title: The Letter I Did Not Send

pages.title: The Letter I Did Not Send
pages.text:
I kept your letter beneath a plate,
as though its weight could settle mine.
The seasons altered; neither name
grew less familiar on the page.

Tonight I write no grand defense,
no verdict on our separate grief.
I leave a margin for your silence
and fold my need to be forgiven.
pages.translation:
나는 당신의 편지를 접시 아래 두었다.
그 무게가 내 마음의 무게를 가라앉힐 수라도 있는 듯.
계절은 바뀌었지만, 종이 위 두 이름은
어느 것도 낯설어지지 않았다.

오늘 밤 나는 거창한 변명도,
우리가 각자 겪은 슬픔에 대한 판결도 쓰지 않는다.
당신의 침묵이 머물 여백을 남기고,
용서받고 싶은 내 마음을 접어 둔다.
pages.scene: Adult literary illustration, a Korean woman in her forties with short dark hair and a plain blue shirt. A quiet kitchen at night, one folded handwritten letter beneath a ceramic plate, blank paper beside it, the woman pausing without posting anything. Indigo shadows and warm amber light.

title: The Weight of an Ordinary Day

pages.title: The Weight of an Ordinary Day
pages.text:
The crowded train delivers us
to separate floors of borrowed light.
I carry bread, a minor ache,
the conversation left unfinished.

At home, a pot breaks the silence.
You move a chair to make me room.
No monument records this kindness.
Its weight is how I know the ground.
pages.translation:
붐비는 기차가 우리를 데려다준다.
빌린 불빛 아래, 저마다 다른 층으로.
나는 빵과 작은 통증,
미처 끝내지 못한 대화를 안고 돌아온다.

집에서는 냄비가 침묵을 깨고,
당신은 의자를 옮겨 내 자리를 만든다.
어떤 기념비도 이 다정함을 기록하지 않는다.
나는 그 무게로 내가 딛고 선 땅을 느낀다.
pages.scene: Adult poetic editorial illustration. A modest apartment at dusk, a tired adult arriving with bread, another adult drawing a chair toward a small kitchen table, a steaming kettle. City train reflected faintly in window, restrained olive and amber.

pages.title: An Empty Line
pages.text: At a gathering, someone asked what I did. My former title rose before my name. I had left the company three months earlier, yet its language still occupied my introduction. Without that familiar status, I felt strangely absent, as though an empty line on a card could erase the person holding it.
pages.translation: 모임에서 누군가 무슨 일을 하느냐고 물었다. 내 이름보다 예전 직함이 먼저 떠올랐다. 회사를 떠난 지 석 달이 지났는데도, 자기소개에는 여전히 회사의 언어가 자리 잡고 있었다. 익숙한 지위가 사라지자 이상하게도 나 자신까지 사라진 기분이었다. 명함의 빈 한 줄이 그것을 쥔 사람까지 지울 수 있는 것처럼.
pages.scene: Reflective adult editorial illustration. Same Korean man in his forties, short dark hair, gray shirt, understated realistic proportions. The man at a small social gathering, holding a plain blank card, listening while other adults converse softly in the background. No visible logos.

pages.title: Other Evidence
pages.text: During that interval, I learned to repair a loose shelf and accompany my father to the clinic. Neither task appeared in my professional profile. Both required patience I had rarely practiced at work. I began to question the narrow criteria through which I had measured a useful life, including the lives of people around me.
pages.translation: 그동안 나는 흔들리는 선반을 고치는 법을 익혔고, 아버지의 병원 진료에 동행했다. 어느 일도 경력 소개에는 들어가지 않았다. 하지만 두 일 모두 직장에서 좀처럼 연습하지 않았던 인내를 요구했다. 나는 쓸모 있는 삶을 재던 좁은 기준에 의문을 품기 시작했다. 그 기준으로 주변 사람들의 삶까지 판단해 왔다는 사실에도.
pages.scene: Reflective adult editorial illustration. Same Korean man in his forties, short dark hair, gray shirt, understated realistic proportions. The man carefully repairing a modest wooden shelf while his elderly father sits nearby with a clinic appointment envelope. Quiet daylight, no medical procedures.

pages.title: A Longer Introduction
pages.text: Work remains important to me. I want fair payment, responsibility, and the chance to acquire expertise. But ambition need not occupy every room. At the next gathering, I offered my name and mentioned the meals I was learning to cook. The conversation continued. An introduction, I discovered, could open a door without displaying a rank.
pages.translation: 일은 여전히 내게 중요하다. 정당한 보수와 책임, 전문성을 쌓을 기회를 원한다. 하지만 야망이 삶의 모든 방을 차지할 필요는 없다. 다음 모임에서는 이름을 말하고, 요즘 배우는 요리 이야기를 덧붙였다. 대화는 자연스럽게 이어졌다. 자기소개는 지위를 내보이지 않고도 문을 열 수 있다는 것을 알게 되었다.
pages.scene: Reflective adult editorial illustration. Same Korean man in his forties, short dark hair, gray shirt, understated realistic proportions. The man sharing a homemade meal at a small gathering, relaxed eye contact with another adult, an open doorway behind them, gentle evening colors.

title: The Life I Did Not Choose

pages.title: The Other Platform
pages.text: An old friend sent a photograph from abroad. For a moment, I inhabited the life I had once considered: another city, another language, a different version of myself. My actual kitchen seemed smaller. Regret is a persuasive editor. It can preserve every attractive detail of an alternative while quietly deleting its uncertain cost.
pages.translation: 오래된 친구가 외국에서 사진을 보내왔다. 잠시 나는 한때 꿈꾸었던 삶 속에 들어갔다. 다른 도시와 언어, 지금과는 다른 나의 모습이었다. 현실의 부엌이 더 좁게 느껴졌다. 후회는 설득력 있는 편집자다. 다른 선택의 매력적인 모습은 남기고, 그 선택에 따랐을 불확실한 대가는 조용히 지워 버린다.
pages.scene: Mature reflective editorial illustration. Same Korean woman in her late thirties, chin-length black hair, rust cardigan. The woman at her kitchen table looking at a small photograph of an unfamiliar city, the actual room warm and modest, imagined station platforms faintly reflected in the window.

pages.title: An Honest Account
pages.text: I wrote two columns, not to prove my choice superior but to restore proportion. One held the opportunities I had abandoned. The other held what staying had allowed: a friendship, steady care for my mother, time to study. Neither column canceled the other. A genuine account could acknowledge loss without declaring the present a failure.
pages.translation: 나는 두 칸으로 나누어 적었다. 내 선택이 더 낫다는 것을 증명하려는 게 아니라, 균형을 되찾고 싶어서였다. 한쪽에는 포기한 기회를, 다른 쪽에는 남았기에 가능했던 것을 적었다. 우정, 어머니를 꾸준히 돌본 시간, 공부할 여유였다. 어느 쪽도 다른 쪽을 지우지 않았다. 정직한 기록이라면 현재를 실패로 단정하지 않으면서도 상실을 인정할 수 있었다.
pages.scene: Mature reflective editorial illustration. Same Korean woman in her late thirties, chin-length black hair, rust cardigan. The woman writing two balanced columns in a notebook, a study book and a family photograph on the table, clear afternoon light. No legible extra writing.

pages.title: Room for a Choice
pages.text: Reconciliation did not arrive as a sudden revelation. I still wondered about that distant city. Yet I could learn its language here, or plan a brief visit when circumstances allowed. Some doors were closed; others required a smaller step. I stopped asking the present to justify every past decision and began asking what remained possible today.
pages.translation: 화해가 갑작스러운 깨달음으로 찾아오지는 않았다. 나는 여전히 그 먼 도시가 궁금했다. 그래도 여기서 그곳의 언어를 배우거나, 형편이 허락할 때 짧은 여행을 계획할 수 있었다. 어떤 문은 닫혔지만, 어떤 문은 더 작은 걸음으로 열 수 있었다. 현재에게 과거의 모든 결정을 정당화하라고 요구하는 대신, 오늘 무엇이 가능한지 묻기 시작했다.
pages.scene: Mature reflective editorial illustration. Same Korean woman in her late thirties, chin-length black hair, rust cardigan. The woman beginning a language lesson beside an open window, a modest travel map folded nearby, dawn light and quiet resolve, no fantasy doorway.

pages.title: A Different Request
pages.text: The shop stored painful memories for a fee. Most clients wanted relief; the older man wanted a withdrawal. He placed a receipt on the table and asked for the afternoon he had surrendered twelve years before. The operator noticed that the account carried a permanent restriction. Beneath it was his own signature.
pages.translation: 그 가게는 비용을 받고 고통스러운 기억을 보관했다. 대부분의 손님은 마음이 가벼워지길 원했지만, 그 노인은 인출을 원했다. 그는 영수증을 내려놓고 열두 해 전 맡긴 어느 오후를 돌려 달라고 했다. 기술자는 그 계정에 영구 제한이 걸려 있음을 발견했다. 그 아래에는 노인 자신의 서명이 있었다.
pages.scene: Original restrained adult science fiction. Same Korean woman technician, forty, short black hair, charcoal jacket; same older Korean man, sixty, gray hair, brown coat. Small municipal memory-storage shop, analog drawers and subtle translucent light, no familiar franchise designs. The older man placing a faded receipt on the counter, the woman technician studying a small terminal, rows of subtle glowing storage drawers.

pages.title: The Restriction
pages.text: She explained that the device could restore a memory only with valid consent. His earlier instruction forbade release to anyone, including himself. He did not dispute the signature. Instead, he asked who had been present that afternoon. The database contained a name, but she could not reveal another person's private information merely because he requested it.
pages.translation: 기술자는 유효한 동의가 있어야 장치가 기억을 복원할 수 있다고 설명했다. 예전 지시는 자신을 포함해 누구에게도 기억을 내주지 말라는 것이었다. 노인은 서명을 부인하지 않았다. 대신 그 오후에 누가 함께 있었는지 물었다. 데이터베이스에는 이름이 있었지만, 그가 원한다는 이유만으로 타인의 사적인 정보를 알려 줄 수는 없었다.
pages.scene: Original restrained adult science fiction. Same Korean woman technician, forty, short black hair, charcoal jacket; same older Korean man, sixty, gray hair, brown coat. Small municipal memory-storage shop, analog drawers and subtle translucent light, no familiar franchise designs. Across the counter the technician gently explains a boundary, the older man listening, a sealed small memory vessel between them, no readable screen text.

pages.title: A Separate Account
pages.text: After he left, she examined the restriction rather than the memory itself. A second account referred to the same incident. Its owner had recently submitted permission for contact. The permission covered one message, not access to either memory. She sent the approved invitation and waited. Two days later, a woman arrived carrying an identical receipt.
pages.translation: 그가 돌아간 뒤 기술자는 기억 자체가 아니라 제한 기록을 살폈다. 다른 계정 하나도 같은 사건을 가리켰다. 그 계정의 주인은 최근 연락을 허용해 두었다. 허용 범위는 메시지 한 건이었고, 어느 쪽 기억에도 접근할 권한은 없었다. 기술자는 승인된 초대를 보냈다. 이틀 뒤 한 여성이 똑같은 영수증을 들고 찾아왔다.
pages.scene: Original restrained adult science fiction. Same Korean woman technician, forty, short black hair, charcoal jacket; same older Korean man, sixty, gray hair, brown coat. Small municipal memory-storage shop, analog drawers and subtle translucent light, no familiar franchise designs. An older Korean woman with gray bob and green coat arrives with a matching receipt, the technician welcoming her, the older man absent.

pages.title: What She Remembered
pages.text: The woman remembered an argument about leaving the family business. Her brother had called her departure a betrayal. She had stored the sound of his voice, not the whole day. For years, each had assumed the other felt nothing. She declined to open his account. She asked whether he would meet her without the device.
pages.translation: 그 여성은 가업을 떠나는 문제로 다투었던 일을 기억했다. 오빠는 자신의 떠남을 배신이라고 불렀다. 그녀가 맡긴 것은 그날 전체가 아니라 오빠의 목소리였다. 오랫동안 두 사람은 상대방에게 아무런 감정도 남아 있지 않다고 생각했다. 그녀는 오빠의 계정을 열지 않겠다고 했다. 장치 없이 만날 의향이 있는지 물어 달라고 했다.
pages.scene: Original restrained adult science fiction. Same Korean woman technician, forty, short black hair, charcoal jacket; same older Korean man, sixty, gray hair, brown coat. Small municipal memory-storage shop, analog drawers and subtle translucent light, no familiar franchise designs. The older woman seated with the technician beside an unpowered memory device, holding a folded receipt, thoughtful dignity rather than melodrama.

pages.title: Two Chairs
pages.text: They met after closing time. The operator placed two chairs near the window and left the storage panel dark. At first they discussed the weather. Then the man admitted he had used the restriction to avoid a decision. He had wanted his regret removed without having to revise the account in which he was right.
pages.translation: 두 사람은 영업이 끝난 뒤 만났다. 기술자는 창가에 의자 두 개를 두고 보관 장치의 화면은 꺼 두었다. 처음에는 날씨 이야기를 했다. 그러다 노인은 결정을 피하려고 제한 지시를 이용했다고 인정했다. 자신이 옳았다는 이야기는 고치지 않은 채, 후회만 없애고 싶었던 것이다.
pages.scene: Original restrained adult science fiction. Same Korean woman technician, forty, short black hair, charcoal jacket; same older Korean man, sixty, gray hair, brown coat. Small municipal memory-storage shop, analog drawers and subtle translucent light, no familiar franchise designs. The older siblings sitting in separate chairs near the shop window at dusk, dark storage panel behind them, technician discreetly at a distance.

pages.title: An Incomplete Record
pages.text: His sister did not offer immediate forgiveness. She described the years in which she had built a life elsewhere. Some were difficult; some were joyful. None appeared in the fragment he wished to recover. A stored memory, the operator said, preserved a perspective. It could not supply the whole truth about another person's life.
pages.translation: 여동생은 곧바로 용서를 말하지 않았다. 다른 곳에서 자신의 삶을 세워 온 세월을 이야기했다. 힘든 때도, 기쁜 때도 있었다. 그 어느 것도 오빠가 되찾으려는 기억 조각에는 들어 있지 않았다. 기술자는 저장된 기억이 하나의 관점을 보존할 뿐, 다른 사람의 삶에 대한 진실 전체를 채워 주지는 못한다고 말했다.
pages.scene: Original restrained adult science fiction. Same Korean woman technician, forty, short black hair, charcoal jacket; same older Korean man, sixty, gray hair, brown coat. Small municipal memory-storage shop, analog drawers and subtle translucent light, no familiar franchise designs. The older woman speaking steadily while her brother listens, a small sealed memory vessel on a side table, warm light on both faces.

pages.title: A New Instruction
pages.text: The man requested a formal examination of his restriction. The shop required a waiting period and an independent witness before any change. He agreed. His sister agreed to receive one letter, with no promise of a reply. Outside, the city continued its ordinary traffic. Nothing in the sky announced that a difficult choice had become possible.
pages.translation: 노인은 자신의 제한 지시를 정식으로 재검토해 달라고 요청했다. 이 가게에서는 변경 전에 대기 기간과 독립된 입회인을 요구했다. 그는 받아들였다. 여동생도 답장을 약속하지는 않은 채 편지 한 통을 받기로 했다. 밖에서는 도시의 평범한 교통이 이어졌다. 어려운 선택이 가능해졌다는 사실을 알리는 표시는 하늘 어디에도 없었다.
pages.scene: Original restrained adult science fiction. Same Korean woman technician, forty, short black hair, charcoal jacket; same older Korean man, sixty, gray hair, brown coat. Small municipal memory-storage shop, analog drawers and subtle translucent light, no familiar franchise designs. The technician handing the man a plain review form while his sister stands near the open shop door, ordinary city traffic outside, no legal symbols.

pages.title: Before the Light
pages.text: During the waiting period, he wrote the letter. He described what he remembered and acknowledged what he could not know. He did not claim a right to a renewed relationship merely because he had suffered. When he returned, the restriction had been lifted through the shop's examination. The operator asked whether he still wished to proceed. He said yes.
pages.translation: 대기 기간 동안 그는 편지를 썼다. 자신이 기억하는 것을 설명하고 알 수 없는 것은 인정했다. 고통을 겪었다고 해서 재회할 권리가 생긴다는 주장도 하지 않았다. 그가 다시 왔을 때, 가게의 검토 절차를 거쳐 제한이 풀려 있었다. 기술자는 그래도 복원을 원하는지 물었다. 그는 그렇다고 답했다.
pages.scene: Original restrained adult science fiction. Same Korean woman technician, forty, short black hair, charcoal jacket; same older Korean man, sixty, gray hair, brown coat. Small municipal memory-storage shop, analog drawers and subtle translucent light, no familiar franchise designs. The older man holding a finished letter beside the technician and a softly lit memory device, hands calm, careful preparation without invasive medical imagery.

pages.title: The Afternoon
pages.text: The memory returned in fragments: a travel bag, rain against a window, his own voice demanding loyalty. Then came a detail he had forgotten. His sister had waited at the door, giving him time to change his words. He had turned away. The device fell silent. He asked for water, and no one tried to interpret his tears.
pages.translation: 기억은 조각으로 돌아왔다. 여행 가방, 창문을 두드리는 비, 충성을 요구하던 자신의 목소리였다. 이어 잊고 있던 장면이 떠올랐다. 여동생은 그가 말을 바꿀 시간을 주며 문 앞에서 기다리고 있었다. 그는 돌아서 버렸다. 장치는 조용해졌다. 그가 물을 달라고 했고, 누구도 그의 눈물에 의미를 붙이려 하지 않았다.
pages.scene: Original restrained adult science fiction. Same Korean woman technician, forty, short black hair, charcoal jacket; same older Korean man, sixty, gray hair, brown coat. Small municipal memory-storage shop, analog drawers and subtle translucent light, no familiar franchise designs. The older man seated safely after a memory session, a glass of water offered by the technician, faint abstract rain and doorway light in background, no literal duplicate characters.

pages.title: A Place to Begin
pages.text: A week later, his sister sent a brief reply. She suggested a walk, not a return to the old business. He folded the letter and kept it in his coat. At the shop, the operator closed the account. On the table lay an empty receipt. For once, the next important moment had not yet been stored.
pages.translation: 일주일 뒤 여동생에게 짧은 답장이 왔다. 옛 사업으로 돌아가자는 말 대신 함께 걷자고 했다. 그는 편지를 접어 외투에 넣었다. 가게에서 기술자는 계정을 닫았다. 계산대에는 아직 아무것도 적히지 않은 영수증이 놓여 있었다. 이번에는 다음의 중요한 순간이 아직 저장되지 않은 채 남아 있었다.
pages.scene: Original restrained adult science fiction. Same Korean woman technician, forty, short black hair, charcoal jacket; same older Korean man, sixty, gray hair, brown coat. Small municipal memory-storage shop, analog drawers and subtle translucent light, no familiar franchise designs. The older siblings walking at a respectful distance along a city riverside in morning light; small inset-like view through shop window of technician closing a drawer, restrained hopeful ending.

pages.title: Closing Time
pages.text: On the final evening, the shopkeeper had already packed the tools when a young man brought in a broken clock. He asked for the repair promised on an old receipt. The date was twenty years earlier. Her father had signed it. She recognized his handwriting, but the address beneath it belonged to a building that no longer existed.
pages.translation: 마지막 영업일 저녁, 주인은 이미 공구를 챙겨 둔 뒤였다. 그때 한 청년이 고장 난 시계를 가져왔다. 그는 오래된 영수증에 약속된 수리를 부탁했다. 날짜는 이십 년 전이었고, 서명은 주인의 아버지 것이었다. 필체는 알아보았지만, 아래 적힌 주소의 건물은 이제 존재하지 않았다.
pages.scene: Original adult realistic mystery, no violence. Same Korean shopkeeper woman fifty, wavy dark hair, beige apron; same young adult Korean man twenty-eight, short black hair, navy coat. Old neighborhood repair shop, brass lamp and wooden counter. The young man setting an old brass clock and faded receipt on a nearly empty repair-shop counter while the woman pauses beside packed tools.

pages.title: The Wrong Number
pages.text: The receipt recorded a deposit larger than the clock's value. The shopkeeper suspected an error. Her father had kept precise accounts, even when the business declined. She found the old journal in a lower box. Beside the payment stood a number that did not correspond to any repair. Someone had drawn a small square around it.
pages.translation: 영수증의 맡긴 돈은 시계 값보다 컸다. 주인은 오류를 의심했다. 아버지는 장사가 기울 때에도 장부를 정확히 썼다. 그녀는 아래쪽 상자에서 옛 장부를 찾았다. 그 금액 옆에는 어떤 수리 내역과도 맞지 않는 번호가 적혀 있었다. 누군가 그 주위에 작은 네모를 그려 놓았다.
pages.scene: Original adult realistic mystery, no violence. Same Korean shopkeeper woman fifty, wavy dark hair, beige apron; same young adult Korean man twenty-eight, short black hair, navy coat. Old neighborhood repair shop, brass lamp and wooden counter. The woman comparing a faded receipt with an old ledger under a brass desk lamp, young man waiting nearby, small boxed mark visible but no readable invented words.

pages.title: An Unfamiliar Key
pages.text: The young man said the clock had belonged to his mother. After her recent move, she had asked him to collect anything still held at the shop. Inside the clock, they discovered a narrow envelope. It contained a key and a second number. The shopkeeper remembered a row of storage boxes in the former building's entrance.
pages.translation: 청년은 어머니의 시계라고 했다. 어머니가 최근 이사한 뒤, 가게에 남겨 둔 것이 있다면 찾아 달라고 부탁했다는 것이다. 두 사람은 시계 안에서 얇은 봉투를 발견했다. 안에는 열쇠와 또 다른 번호가 있었다. 주인은 사라진 건물 입구에 늘어서 있던 보관함을 떠올렸다.
pages.scene: Original adult realistic mystery, no violence. Same Korean shopkeeper woman fifty, wavy dark hair, beige apron; same young adult Korean man twenty-eight, short black hair, navy coat. Old neighborhood repair shop, brass lamp and wooden counter. Open back of the brass clock revealing a narrow envelope and small key on the counter, both adults examining it thoughtfully, no mechanical fantasy.

pages.title: What Remained
pages.text: The building had been removed, but its former manager still lived nearby. With the mother's permission, they asked about the boxes. The manager had preserved several unclaimed items during the move. One box matched the key. Inside lay a bundle of letters and a photograph of the shopkeeper's father standing beside a woman she did not recognize.
pages.translation: 건물은 없어졌지만 예전 관리인은 근처에 살고 있었다. 어머니의 허락을 받고 두 사람은 보관함을 물었다. 관리인은 이전할 때 찾아가지 않은 물건 몇 개를 보관해 두었다. 열쇠에 맞는 상자가 하나 있었다. 안에는 편지 묶음과 사진 한 장이 있었다. 아버지가 낯선 여성 곁에 서 있었다.
pages.scene: Original adult realistic mystery, no violence. Same Korean shopkeeper woman fifty, wavy dark hair, beige apron; same young adult Korean man twenty-eight, short black hair, navy coat. Old neighborhood repair shop, brass lamp and wooden counter. An elderly manager presenting a small wooden storage box, letters and a faded photograph inside, the shopkeeper and young man together in a modest sitting room.

pages.title: A Familiar Face
pages.text: The young man identified the woman as his mother. The shopkeeper studied her father's expression and felt an unwelcome suspicion. Had the deposit concealed a secret relationship? The letters might answer, but they were addressed to the mother. She returned them unopened. The young man called home and asked whether they could come by the following morning.
pages.translation: 청년은 사진 속 여성이 어머니라고 했다. 주인은 아버지의 표정을 보며 달갑지 않은 의심에 사로잡혔다. 맡긴 돈에 비밀스러운 관계가 숨겨져 있었을까? 편지가 답을 줄지도 몰랐지만, 수신인은 청년의 어머니였다. 그녀는 뜯지 않은 채 돌려주었다. 청년은 집에 전화해 다음 날 아침 함께 찾아가도 되는지 물었다.
pages.scene: Original adult realistic mystery, no violence. Same Korean shopkeeper woman fifty, wavy dark hair, beige apron; same young adult Korean man twenty-eight, short black hair, navy coat. Old neighborhood repair shop, brass lamp and wooden counter. The woman looking at an old photograph then handing sealed letters back to the young man, who makes a phone call near the window. Respectful tension, no sinister shadows.

pages.title: The Account
pages.text: His mother read the letters before they arrived. Years earlier, she had helped the father organize deliveries while recovering from an injury. The money recorded as a deposit was payment he owed her, held at her request while she lacked a safe place to keep it. The clock was their private reminder. Then illness had interrupted their contact, leaving the account unresolved.
pages.translation: 어머니는 두 사람이 오기 전에 편지를 읽었다. 오래전 그녀는 부상에서 회복하는 동안 주인의 아버지를 도와 배달 업무를 정리했다. 맡긴 돈으로 기록된 그 금액은 아버지가 지급해야 할 보수였다. 안전하게 보관할 곳이 없어 그녀의 요청으로 맡겨 둔 돈이었다. 시계는 두 사람 사이의 표시였다. 그러다 병으로 연락이 끊기면서 정산도 끝나지 못했다.
pages.scene: Original adult realistic mystery, no violence. Same Korean shopkeeper woman fifty, wavy dark hair, beige apron; same young adult Korean man twenty-eight, short black hair, navy coat. Old neighborhood repair shop, brass lamp and wooden counter. Young man's mother, a Korean woman sixty with short gray hair and green sweater, explaining open letters at her kitchen table to the two visitors, morning light.

pages.title: A Different Debt
pages.text: The shopkeeper asked why no one had claimed the money later. The mother explained that a relative had managed her affairs during a long illness. She had only recently found the receipt among returned papers. The shopkeeper felt relief, then embarrassment. She had been ready to invent a scandal before asking the person whose life the papers concerned.
pages.translation: 주인은 나중에도 돈을 찾지 않은 이유를 물었다. 어머니는 오래 앓는 동안 친척이 자기 일을 맡았다고 설명했다. 돌려받은 서류에서 영수증을 찾은 것도 최근이었다. 주인은 안도한 뒤 부끄러워졌다. 그 기록이 가리키는 삶의 당사자에게 묻기도 전에 추문부터 만들어 내려고 했던 것이다.
pages.scene: Original adult realistic mystery, no violence. Same Korean shopkeeper woman fifty, wavy dark hair, beige apron; same young adult Korean man twenty-eight, short black hair, navy coat. Old neighborhood repair shop, brass lamp and wooden counter. The shopkeeper listening with lowered eyes and a thoughtful expression, the older woman calmly holding the recovered receipt, young man seated between them, no exaggerated emotion.

pages.title: The Next Page
pages.text: Back at the shop, the journal's next page resolved the payment. Her father had transferred the money to a separate account and recorded the reference. The deposit remained there. She contacted the bank with the mother rather than promising an immediate payment she could not approve. The process would take time. For once, delay protected someone instead of dismissing them.
pages.translation: 가게로 돌아와 보니 장부의 다음 쪽에 돈의 행방이 적혀 있었다. 아버지는 별도 계좌로 돈을 옮기고 조회 번호를 남겼다. 돈은 그곳에 남아 있었다. 주인은 자신이 승인할 수 없는 즉시 지급을 약속하는 대신 어머니와 함께 은행에 연락했다. 절차에는 시간이 필요했다. 이번의 기다림은 누군가를 밀어내는 대신 보호하는 것이었다.
pages.scene: Original adult realistic mystery, no violence. Same Korean shopkeeper woman fifty, wavy dark hair, beige apron; same young adult Korean man twenty-eight, short black hair, navy coat. Old neighborhood repair shop, brass lamp and wooden counter. The shopkeeper and older mother together at the repair-shop counter making a bank call with open ledger and receipt, orderly paperwork, no readable account numbers.

pages.title: One More Repair
pages.text: Before the tools were packed again, the shopkeeper repaired the clock. A loose connection, not a ruined mechanism, had stopped it. The young man asked what he owed. She showed him a new receipt with the ordinary charge. Neither charity nor guilt needed to conceal the price. He paid, and the clock marked the hour once more.
pages.translation: 공구를 다시 챙기기 전에 주인은 시계를 고쳤다. 장치가 망가진 게 아니라 연결 부위가 느슨해져 멈춘 것이었다. 청년이 얼마냐고 묻자 그녀는 보통 수리비가 적힌 새 영수증을 내밀었다. 호의도 죄책감도 가격을 숨길 필요는 없었다. 청년이 돈을 냈고, 시계는 다시 시간을 알렸다.
pages.scene: Original adult realistic mystery, no violence. Same Korean shopkeeper woman fifty, wavy dark hair, beige apron; same young adult Korean man twenty-eight, short black hair, navy coat. Old neighborhood repair shop, brass lamp and wooden counter. The woman using a small hand tool to finish the brass clock repair while the young man waits, fresh receipt beside the clock, warm clear lamplight.

pages.title: After the Door
pages.text: A month later, the mother confirmed that the account had been settled. By then, the shop was empty. The shopkeeper kept the old journal, but not as proof that her father had been flawless. It reminded her how easily an incomplete record could become an accusation. In her new kitchen, a modest clock continued its work. She listened, then opened the window.
pages.translation: 한 달 뒤 어머니는 정산이 끝났다고 알려왔다. 그때 가게는 이미 비어 있었다. 주인은 옛 장부를 간직했다. 아버지가 흠없는 사람이었다는 증거로 삼으려는 것은 아니었다. 불완전한 기록이 얼마나 쉽게 비난으로 변하는지를 기억하기 위해서였다. 새집 부엌에서는 소박한 시계가 제 일을 하고 있었다. 그녀는 그 소리를 듣다가 창문을 열었다.
pages.scene: Original adult realistic mystery, no violence. Same Korean shopkeeper woman fifty, wavy dark hair, beige apron; same young adult Korean man twenty-eight, short black hair, navy coat. Old neighborhood repair shop, brass lamp and wooden counter. The shopkeeper without apron in her new modest kitchen, old closed ledger on a shelf, a different simple wall clock, opening a window toward morning, quiet resolution.

pages.title: The Claim
pages.text: In an imaginary city, a small printing company faced a claim for a severe contract penalty. The owner had signed a delivery schedule she believed included a revision. The buyer produced a copy without it. Her signature appeared genuine on both versions. At the first hearing, the judge asked which document had governed the agreement, not which company seemed more sympathetic.
pages.translation: 가상의 도시에서 작은 인쇄 회사가 거액의 계약 위약금을 청구당했다. 사장은 수정 내용이 포함되어 있다고 믿고 납품 일정표에 서명했다. 구매 업체는 수정 내용이 없는 사본을 내놓았다. 두 문서의 서명은 모두 진짜로 보였다. 첫 심리에서 판사는 어느 회사가 더 동정할 만한지가 아니라 어떤 문서에 합의했는지 물었다.
pages.scene: Original adult courtroom drama in an explicitly imaginary city, invented civil procedure. Same Korean woman small-business owner forty-five, shoulder-length black hair, navy suit; her counsel Korean woman forty, short hair, gray suit; witness Korean man thirty-five, glasses, brown jacket. Generic modest courtroom with single judge, no jury, no national flags, no real legal insignia or readable legal text. The owner and her counsel seated at a courtroom table with two document folders, buyer represented across the room, neutral judge listening. Quiet civil dispute, no handcuffs.

pages.title: Two Versions
pages.text: The owner's counsel compared the copies. The final page was identical; the delivery clause on the preceding page was not. The contract had arrived as an electronic file, then been printed for signature. The owner remembered a hurried meeting and a colleague replacing a sheet. Memory alone could not establish when the replacement occurred or whether the buyer had approved it.
pages.translation: 사장의 대리인은 두 사본을 비교했다. 마지막 쪽은 같았지만 앞쪽의 납품 조항은 달랐다. 계약서는 전자 파일로 온 뒤 서명을 위해 출력되었다. 사장은 급하게 진행된 회의와 동료가 종이 한 장을 바꾸던 일을 기억했다. 그러나 기억만으로는 언제 바뀌었는지, 구매 업체가 승인했는지 밝힐 수 없었다.
pages.scene: Original adult courtroom drama in an explicitly imaginary city, invented civil procedure. Same Korean woman small-business owner forty-five, shoulder-length black hair, navy suit; her counsel Korean woman forty, short hair, gray suit; witness Korean man thirty-five, glasses, brown jacket. Generic modest courtroom with single judge, no jury, no national flags, no real legal insignia or readable legal text. Counsel examining two sets of printed pages beside a laptop at a quiet office table, owner pointing carefully, contrasting page arrangements without legible wording.

pages.title: The Witness
pages.text: The colleague agreed to give evidence. He recalled receiving an updated file before the meeting. Yet he had left the company after a dispute about wages. The buyer's counsel questioned his motive. He admitted his resentment but refused to claim certainty he lacked. He remembered printing the file. He could not remember who had carried the pages into the room.
pages.translation: 동료는 증언하기로 했다. 회의 전에 갱신된 파일을 받았다고 기억했다. 하지만 그는 임금 문제로 다툰 뒤 회사를 떠난 상태였다. 구매 업체의 대리인은 증언 동기를 따졌다. 그는 불만이 있다는 사실은 인정했지만, 확신할 수 없는 일을 단정하지 않았다. 파일을 출력한 것은 기억해도, 누가 종이를 회의실로 가져갔는지는 기억하지 못했다.
pages.scene: Original adult courtroom drama in an explicitly imaginary city, invented civil procedure. Same Korean woman small-business owner forty-five, shoulder-length black hair, navy suit; her counsel Korean woman forty, short hair, gray suit; witness Korean man thirty-five, glasses, brown jacket. Generic modest courtroom with single judge, no jury, no national flags, no real legal insignia or readable legal text. The witness standing at a simple witness desk, speaking thoughtfully to the judge while counsel listens, owner seated in background, no dramatic pointing.

pages.title: The Question
pages.text: Under further questioning, the witness conceded that the printer's clock had been inaccurate. A time recorded on the print log could not settle the sequence. The owner felt her case collapse. Her counsel asked for the original records rather than a convenient conclusion. An error could weaken one inference without making every other piece of evidence false.
pages.translation: 이어진 질문에서 증인은 프린터의 시계가 정확하지 않았다고 인정했다. 출력 기록의 시간만으로는 사건 순서를 확정할 수 없었다. 사장은 자신의 주장이 무너지는 듯했다. 대리인은 편리한 결론 대신 원본 기록을 요청했다. 한 오류가 하나의 추론을 약하게 만들 수는 있어도, 다른 증거까지 모두 거짓으로 만들지는 않았다.
pages.scene: Original adult courtroom drama in an explicitly imaginary city, invented civil procedure. Same Korean woman small-business owner forty-five, shoulder-length black hair, navy suit; her counsel Korean woman forty, short hair, gray suit; witness Korean man thirty-five, glasses, brown jacket. Generic modest courtroom with single judge, no jury, no national flags, no real legal insignia or readable legal text. Witness acknowledging uncertainty with a calm open hand, counsel studying a printer log in a folder, owner concerned but composed, judge attentive.

pages.title: A Separate Record
pages.text: The original message records contained an attachment with the revised clause. A reply from the buyer's office acknowledged receipt, but receipt was not necessarily consent. The judge permitted both sides to examine the record under the city's fictional procedure. The buyer's counsel pointed out that the reply had come from an assistant without permission to approve contract changes.
pages.translation: 원본 메시지 보관 기록에는 수정 조항이 담긴 첨부 파일이 있었다. 구매 업체의 사무실에서 수신 확인 답장을 보냈지만, 받았다는 것이 반드시 동의를 뜻하지는 않았다. 판사는 이 도시의 가상 절차에 따라 양측이 기록을 살피게 했다. 구매 업체 측은 답장을 보낸 직원에게 계약 변경 승인 권한이 없다고 지적했다.
pages.scene: Original adult courtroom drama in an explicitly imaginary city, invented civil procedure. Same Korean woman small-business owner forty-five, shoulder-length black hair, navy suit; her counsel Korean woman forty, short hair, gray suit; witness Korean man thirty-five, glasses, brown jacket. Generic modest courtroom with single judge, no jury, no national flags, no real legal insignia or readable legal text. Both counsel examining a digital record displayed privately on a laptop at the courtroom table, judge in background, no readable screen or jurisdictional symbols.

pages.title: The Owner's Admission
pages.text: Then the owner faced a difficult question. Had her company met even the revised schedule? It had not. She acknowledged a delay of two days and the cost it had imposed on the buyer. Her counsel did not interrupt. Defending against an excessive claim did not require presenting her company as innocent of every failure.
pages.translation: 이어서 사장은 어려운 질문을 받았다. 수정된 일정만큼은 지켰는가? 그렇지 못했다. 그녀는 이틀의 지연과 그것이 구매 업체에 발생시킨 비용을 인정했다. 대리인은 말을 끊지 않았다. 과도한 청구에 맞서기 위해 자신의 회사가 모든 잘못에서 결백하다고 꾸밀 필요는 없었다.
pages.scene: Original adult courtroom drama in an explicitly imaginary city, invented civil procedure. Same Korean woman small-business owner forty-five, shoulder-length black hair, navy suit; her counsel Korean woman forty, short hair, gray suit; witness Korean man thirty-five, glasses, brown jacket. Generic modest courtroom with single judge, no jury, no national flags, no real legal insignia or readable legal text. The owner giving a composed candid answer at the witness desk, her counsel listening without interruption, buyer's representative attentive, understated tension.

pages.title: The Relevant Detail
pages.text: A delivery receipt revealed a further detail. The buyer had accepted an initial portion of the order after the original agreed date and requested the remainder on the revised date. That conduct supported the owner's account, although it did not explain every conversation. Both sides questioned the employee who had sent the request. The employee confirmed the instruction came from the buyer's manager.
pages.translation: 납품 확인서에서 새로운 사실이 드러났다. 구매 업체는 원래 기한이 지난 뒤 첫 물량을 받고, 나머지는 수정된 날짜에 보내 달라고 요청했다. 그 행동은 사장의 설명을 뒷받침했지만 모든 대화를 설명하지는 못했다. 양측은 요청을 보낸 직원을 질문했다. 직원은 구매 업체 관리자의 지시였다고 확인했다.
pages.scene: Original adult courtroom drama in an explicitly imaginary city, invented civil procedure. Same Korean woman small-business owner forty-five, shoulder-length black hair, navy suit; her counsel Korean woman forty, short hair, gray suit; witness Korean man thirty-five, glasses, brown jacket. Generic modest courtroom with single judge, no jury, no national flags, no real legal insignia or readable legal text. A new employee witness, Korean woman thirty in a plain cream blouse, explaining a delivery receipt, both counsel with orderly folders, generic courtroom continuity.

pages.title: Final Arguments
pages.text: In her final argument, counsel distinguished the disputed penalty from the admitted delay. She asked the court to evaluate the documents and conduct together, and to recognize the buyer's demonstrated loss. Across the room, the buyer's counsel defended the earlier schedule. Neither argument could restore the trust that hurried meetings and incomplete records had already damaged.
pages.translation: 최종 변론에서 대리인은 다투는 위약금과 인정한 지연을 구분했다. 문서와 행동을 함께 평가하고 구매 업체가 입증한 손해도 인정해 달라고 요청했다. 반대편에서는 구매 업체의 대리인이 원래 일정을 주장했다. 어느 변론도 성급한 회의와 불완전한 기록이 이미 훼손한 신뢰를 되돌릴 수는 없었다.
pages.scene: Original adult courtroom drama in an explicitly imaginary city, invented civil procedure. Same Korean woman small-business owner forty-five, shoulder-length black hair, navy suit; her counsel Korean woman forty, short hair, gray suit; witness Korean man thirty-five, glasses, brown jacket. Generic modest courtroom with single judge, no jury, no national flags, no real legal insignia or readable legal text. Owner's counsel delivering a restrained final argument from beside her table, two sets of documents aligned, buyer's counsel across the room, judge listening in soft daylight.

pages.title: The Decision
pages.text: The judge concluded that the parties had adopted the revised schedule through their documented conduct. The severe penalty claim failed, but the printing company remained liable for the loss caused by its later delay. The owner heard both parts. Outside, her colleague asked whether she called that a victory. She said she needed time to decide what the word meant.
pages.translation: 판사는 기록으로 확인되는 양측의 행동을 통해 수정 일정이 채택되었다고 판단했다. 거액의 위약금 청구는 받아들여지지 않았지만, 인쇄 회사는 그 뒤의 지연으로 발생한 손해를 책임져야 했다. 사장은 두 부분을 모두 들었다. 밖에서 동료가 승리라고 생각하느냐고 묻자, 그녀는 그 말의 뜻을 생각할 시간이 필요하다고 답했다.
pages.scene: Original adult courtroom drama in an explicitly imaginary city, invented civil procedure. Same Korean woman small-business owner forty-five, shoulder-length black hair, navy suit; her counsel Korean woman forty, short hair, gray suit; witness Korean man thirty-five, glasses, brown jacket. Generic modest courtroom with single judge, no jury, no national flags, no real legal insignia or readable legal text. The owner and former colleague outside the generic courthouse on ordinary stone steps, each holding a folder, reflective rather than celebrating, no national architecture or press crowd.

pages.title: The Next Signature
pages.text: Back at the workshop, she changed the contract examination process. Revised pages would carry clear dates; approval would be recorded before work began. She also paid the wages still owed to her former colleague. On the next agreement, her hand paused above the signature line. The pen was ordinary. What it committed other people to endure was not.
pages.translation: 작업장으로 돌아온 그녀는 계약 검토 절차를 바꿨다. 수정된 쪽에는 날짜를 분명히 쓰고, 일을 시작하기 전에 승인을 기록하기로 했다. 옛 동료에게 남아 있던 임금도 지급했다. 다음 계약서에서 그녀의 손은 서명란 위에 잠시 멈췄다. 펜은 평범했다. 그러나 그 펜이 다른 사람들에게 감당하게 할 일은 가볍지 않았다.
pages.scene: Original adult courtroom drama in an explicitly imaginary city, invented civil procedure. Same Korean woman small-business owner forty-five, shoulder-length black hair, navy suit; her counsel Korean woman forty, short hair, gray suit; witness Korean man thirty-five, glasses, brown jacket. Generic modest courtroom with single judge, no jury, no national flags, no real legal insignia or readable legal text. The owner at her printing-workshop desk pausing with a pen above a new agreement, clear organized page tabs, printing equipment softly in background, quiet responsible ending.
